items.title: Iran says US proposal narrowed gaps but uranium, toll disputes persist

featured_image.name: Iran Says the US's Latest Proposal Has 'Narrowed the Gaps' - Bloomberg

items.description: Iran indicated on Thursday that the latest American proposal has partially reduced differences between the two sides, even as it prepares a formal response to a plan that would see the Strait of Hormuz reopened and the US naval blockade of Iranian ports lifted. However, a dispute over Iran's push for a permanent toll system in the waterway and Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei's reported refusal to surrender Tehran's enriched uranium stockpile threaten to derail progress toward a lasting peace.

items.title: Iran says US proposal 'narrowed the gaps' as House eyes war powers vote

featured_image.name: WATCH LIVE: House expected to vote on Senate resolution to ... - PBS

items.description:
Iran said Wednesday it is reviewing Washington's latest response to its peace proposal aimed at ending the nearly three-month conflict, as President Donald Trump warned that negotiations are on the "borderline" between a deal and renewed strikes.

The Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said Tehran had "received the US perspectives and is in the process of reviewing them," according to the Iranian state news agency Nour News. Iran also said the latest US proposal had "narrowed the gaps" between the two sides.[1][2][3]

items.title: Lithuania confirms crashed drone was Ukrainian

featured_image.name: Lithuania's leaders take shelter during drone air alert

items.description:
A suspected drone entering Lithuanian airspace from Belarus on Wednesday triggered the first air alert in an EU and NATO capital to order civilian shelters since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, forcing President Gitanas Nausėda, Prime Minister Inga Ruginienė, and members of parliament into bunkers while Vilnius Airport suspended flights and train services were halted.[1][2][3]

The alert, sent to mobile phones at around 10:20 a.m. local time, read: "Air raid alert! Go immediately to a shelter or a safe place, take care of your family members and wait for further instructions". Within minutes, residents across the capital descended into basements and underground parking garages. "I got dressed and went down to the basement," photographer Andrej Vasilenko told AFP. "My child was at school and had gone down into a shelter, so I felt reassured. It was strange, but at the same time so many people in Ukraine have been living with this for four years".[3]

items.title: Iran seeks permanent Hormuz toll system in talks with Oman

featured_image.name: Iran, Oman To Set Hormuz Toll Together - Iran Press

items.description:
Iran is in active discussions with Oman to establish a permanent toll system for maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, seeking to formalize what has been an ad hoc fee regime since the conflict with the United States and Israel erupted earlier this year.

Iranian Ambassador to France Mohammad Amin-Nejad told Bloomberg on Wednesday that "Iran and Oman must mobilize all their resources both to provide security services and to manage navigation in the most appropriate manner." The statement represents Tehran's clearest articulation yet of its intent to make the toll arrangement a lasting feature of Gulf commerce rather than a wartime stopgap.[1]

items.title: Iran restarted drone production during ceasefire, US intelligence finds

featured_image.name: Iran opens military drone factory in Tajikistan

items.description:
Iran has restarted drone production during the six-week ceasefire that began in early April, rebuilding its military industrial base at a pace that has caught US intelligence agencies off guard, CNN reported Thursday citing four sources familiar with the assessments.[1][2]

The reporting contradicts weeks of public assurances from Trump administration officials and military leaders who characterized Iran's military as crippled beyond near-term repair following Operation Epic Fury, the US-Israeli bombing campaign that began in late February.

items.title: Turkey sends flights to repatriate Gaza flotilla activists detained by Israel

featured_image.name: Flotilla activists return to Istanbul after Israel detains them at sea

items.description:
Israel has begun deporting approximately 430 activists detained from the Global Sumud Flotilla after Israeli naval forces intercepted the Gaza-bound aid convoy in international waters west of Cyprus, a move that has triggered a wave of international condemnation intensified by a video posted by far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir showing him taunting bound detainees.

The deportations, confirmed on Wednesday, follow days of mounting diplomatic fallout after Ben-Gvir shared footage of himself confronting kneeling activists with their hands zip-tied behind their backs, waving an Israeli flag and reportedly shouting "We are the masters" as Israel's national anthem played in the background. Turkey said on Thursday it was sending charter flights to Israel to repatriate its nationals among the detained activists.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Merz proposes EU 'associate membership' for Ukraine

featured_image.name: Merz rules out 'immediate' EU membership for Ukraine, proposes Kyiv attend  meetings

items.description:
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has formally proposed granting Ukraine "associate member" status in the European Union, outlining the plan in a letter to EU chiefs Ursula von der Leyen and António Costa made public on Thursday.[1][2]

The proposal would allow Ukraine's leader to attend EU summits and ministerial meetings without voting rights, while Kyiv would also gain a non-voting representative on the European Commission and non-voting members of the European Parliament.[2][1]

items.title: Ukrainian drone strikes bring central Russia's oil refining to a standstill

featured_image.name: 2 Russian oil refineries cut production after Ukrainian drone attacks,  Reuters reports

items.description: A sustained campaign of Ukrainian drone strikes has forced virtually all major oil refineries in central Russia to halt or scale back fuel production, bringing refining operations across the region to a near-standstill, Reuters reported on May 20. The disruptions mark one of the most concentrated blows to Russian energy infrastructure since the start of the full-scale war.[1][2]

items.title: Beijing delays Pentagon official's visit over Taiwan arms deal

featured_image.name: Pentagon official's Beijing visit in doubt over $14 billion US arms package for Taiwan, FT reports

items.description:
Beijing is stalling a planned visit by Elbridge Colby, the Pentagon's under-secretary of defense for policy, as China pressures President Donald Trump over a $14 billion weapons package for Taiwan, according to a Financial Times report published Wednesday.[1]

The delay comes just days after Trump's two-day summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing on May 14-15, during which Taiwan emerged as one of the most contentious issues. Reuters was unable to independently confirm the details of the FT report.[2][3][1]
